pageTitle: KKTerm — One window for terminals, SSH, SFTP, RDP, VNC, and an AI that builds you tools
supportBanner: Support independent development with a store purchase. One-time payment, no subscription.
heroTitle: One native window for every terminal, SSH, SFTP, RDP, and VNC connection you own.
heroDescription: KKTerm replaces the pile of clients on your taskbar — terminal, SSH, SFTP, RDP, VNC, an embedded browser, a file manager — with one workspace. Plus an AI assistant that acts on your sessions, with a human in the approval loop.
appleDownload: Download on the Mac App Store
supportNote: 💚 Support independent development: the store editions fund the same KKTerm you get free on GitHub — a one-time payment, no subscription. Every purchase goes straight back into bug fixes, new features, and signed, auto-updating releases.
heroCaption: Real KKTerm capture · Maelstrom terminal background
connectionsDescription: Same app. Same window. Same hotkeys. No more alt-tabbing through a decade of separate tools.
localTerminalDescription: PowerShell, cmd, and WSL shells, side by side.
sshDescription: Keys, agent, passwords, jump hosts, port forwarding.
sftpDescription: Dual-pane file browser, drag to transfer.
serialDescription: Ancient gear and COM-port devices, still welcome.
rdpDescription: The real Microsoft Remote Desktop, built right in.
vncDescription: Rendered straight into the workspace canvas.
browserDescription: A router's admin UI, one tab away, saved logins.
filesDescription: Local disk browsing plus a log/CSV/image/PDF viewer with tail-follow.
aiTitle: An assistant that commands your terminals — with you watching
aiDescription: Most "AI in your terminal" demos stop at chat. KKTerm's assistant works inside your session: hand it context from whatever is already on screen, and it acts on the boxes you're connected to.
aiHistory: Pull live terminal scrollback straight into the conversation
aiScreenshot: Screenshot a Pane and ask "why does this look wrong?"
aiApproval: Every risky command is flagged and waits for an explicit yes
aiModels: Bring your own model — OpenAI, Gemini, Grok, Ollama, Claude Code CLI, Codex CLI, and more
dashboardTitle: A dashboard that doesn't pretend to be Grafana
dashboardDescription: Describe a widget in plain English and the AI assistant builds it, live, on your grid — in its own sandbox, with your approval. No marketplace, no JavaScript required.
widgetCommits: "Add a widget showing the last 5 commits on my main repo as a list."
widgetPing: "Build a widget that pings my home router every 30 seconds and shows green/red."
widgetCustomize: Drag, resize, re-color. Delete one with a right-click when the magic wears off.
tmuxTitle: Keep your AI agents alive across a dropped Wi-Fi
tmuxDescription: Open an SSH connection with tmux enabled, start claude or codex, close the laptop, open it again — the pane silently re-attaches. Still running. Still has its scrollback. Still in the middle of whatever it was doing.
psmuxDescription: Local PowerShell panes get the same trick on Windows through psmux, the native tmux clone.
workspacesTitle: Workspaces for the home lab, the day job, and that one client
workspacesDescription: Workspaces are named, isolated containers of Connections you switch between from the Activity Rail. Switching re-scopes the Connection Tree only — your open Sessions, Dashboard, and Settings stay put. Changing context costs one click, not a relaunch.
panesDescription: Inside a Workspace, a Tab can hold a grid of mixed Panes: SSH next to SFTP, a local shell below an RDP session, VNC beside a file browser.
operationsTitle: Operate the fleet, capture the evidence
operationsDescription: The same local workspace also covers repeatable IT work and the screenshots or recordings that explain what happened.
itopsSubtitle: Sites, racks, tasks, and batch runs
itopsDescription: Model rooms and racks, bind Connections to Hosts, scan endpoints, and fan out reusable tasks over SSH with saved run reports.
screenshotsDescription: Grab a region, window, or full screen; organize the library; annotate images; and record silent MP4, WebM, or GIF clips with FFmpeg.
gitDescription: Inspect history, stage changes, and compare text, folders, hex, or images without leaving the app.
modulesDescription: Install optional .kkmod tools that add isolated destinations to the Activity Rail.
secretsDescription: Keep durable data in SQLite, passwords in the OS keychain, and export selective or full backups.
languagesDescription: Run the full app in English, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and ten more locales.
customizeDescription: Color themes restyle the whole app chrome; animated backgrounds run behind any dashboard view or terminal pane — yes, including matrix. Both pause when you're elsewhere, so they cost roughly nothing.
installerTitle: Install Helper: a fresh box, set up without ten browser tabs
installerDescription: A built-in catalog that finds, installs, updates, and uninstalls the tools you'd otherwise chase by hand — Node, Python, Git, Claude Code, Codex, WSL, PowerToys, and more. UAC prompts stay explicit; nothing installs silently.
installerPlatforms: macOS and Linux already have package managers you love, so this one stays a Windows-only convenience.
noCloudDescription: No sync, no team accounts, no SaaS tier. A "sign in to KKTerm" dialog would mean something went catastrophically wrong.
noAutonomyDescription: The assistant proposes; the human disposes. "Allow All" is a choice you make, not a default.
noGrafanaDescription: The Dashboard is for personal control surfaces, not 10k-host observability.
platformDifferencesTitle: Not pretending every OS is identical
platformDifferencesDescription: Windows, macOS, and Linux builds ship, but platform-specific features stay honest about what's native and what isn't.
storyTitle: Named after a snack that keeps servers well-behaved
storyDescription: Walk into a data center in Taiwan and look at the top of the racks — you'll spot a small green bag of 乖乖 (Kuāi Kuāi), a coconut-flavored corn snack from the 1960s. The name means “be good, behave.” Engineers place it on equipment as a good-luck charm: it must be green (coconut, never spicy red or curry yellow), it must be unexpired, and it must never be eaten. That bag is on duty.
storyPurpose: KKTerm — Kuai Kuai Term — aims for the same job: sit quietly next to your important machines and help them behave. Local-first. No telemetry. Approval-gated AI. The boring, dependable kind of software.
downloadDescription: The kindest way to get KKTerm — and keep it alive — is a store edition: one-time payment, no subscription, with signed packaging and automatic updates. Every purchase funds continued development.
storePayment: One-time payment, no subscription. Signed and auto-updating.
storeLimitations: Honest limitations: the Mac App Store build runs inside Apple's App Sandbox — local shells are confined (container home, no dotfiles or Homebrew tools; remote SSH is unaffected), real folders need a one-time picker grant, and video recording plus the shutdown-timer menu are unavailable. The Microsoft Store build is the full Windows app with a 7-day trial option. Both update through their store.
githubHelp: For Linux, free builds, source code, and documentation, use GitHub in the top-right header.
